notes: Schedule 1-A Part V line 36a: line 35 when the taxpayer was born before January 2, 1961 (tax.us.2025.taxpayer-over-65, same fact and meaning the standard deduction rule reads -- P0 Sec. 1/3), has a valid SSN, and the return is not married filing separately (f1040s1a-2025 line 36a caption; i1040gi-2025 p.109 'If you are married, you must file a joint return ... to claim this deduction'); otherwise 0, never blocked, so a non-qualifying return (most returns: not 65 or older) always publishes a genuine zero that line 37 can sum. The valid-SSN answer is required only when the taxpayer is recorded as 65 or older and the return is not MFS (tax.us.2025.senior-deduction.taxpayer-valid-ssn as a conditional_dependency_set member, per ADR-0037/ADR-0038): a return with no one 65 or older, or an MFS return, computes without ever being asked for it, matching the contract's 'a question is required only where its answer can change the result.' A senior who is asked and leaves it unanswered blocks DEPENDENCY_ABSENT naming the fact; a senior who answers 'no' (invalid or missing SSN) is not blocked -- line 36a is a genuine, published $0 for that person, same posture as the SSN-less spouse in the plan's joint-SSN case.
